task: Point two-stage FX backtest at self-hosted Laya (open-source Jev substitute) and run it
what_went_wrong: A 15h04m backtest run (7 pair shards, 40,210 Laya calls, 0 HTTP errors) produced results in which the three Jev-dependent strategies are invalid artifacts. `regimeOnly` is numerically identical to `momentumOnly` and `twoStage` identical to `jevMomentumFilter` in all 7 pairs: regime cache = 18,571/18,571 TRENDING, direction cache = 99.0% 'up'.
root_cause: The substituted runtime's fitness for the task was assumed from wire-format compatibility and never measured at the decision level. Laya's base checkpoint has no zero-shot discriminative signal on the backtest's numeric-only FX prompts (its own model card warns the base checkpoints are near chance and are 'a fast base to specialise, not a zero-shot decision engine'). A pre-flight smoke test on a convenient payload shape passed while the production ask was unanswerable.
evidence: Order-swap probe, identical unambiguous 20-day downtrend state: (A) dict instructions, UP listed first -> choice=UP, probabilities 0.5227/0.4773, confidence 0.0015 (near-tie, no signal). (B) dict instructions, DOWN listed first -> choice=DOWN, 0.8633. Same state, answer followed option ORDER.

(C) string instructions, UP first -> choice=DOWN 0.815; (D) string instructions, DOWN first -> choice=DOWN 0.9115. State-driven and order-independent - but ONLY because that probe's state contained the explicit sentence 'The price has fallen every day for 20 days straight'.
Production cache truth: cache/regime-<pair>.json = 2653 entries all 'TRENDING' for all 7 pairs; cache/direction-<pair>.json = 2575-2649 'up' vs 4-78 'down'.
Consequence: regime detection never returned MEAN_REVERTING, so regimeOnly == momentumOnly and twoStage == jevMomentumFilter exactly.
impact: The Jev-dependent conclusions of the two-stage backtest are unsupported. The API-free strategies (buyAndHold, momentumOnly) are unaffected and valid. ~15h of compute spent producing unusable Jev numbers.
correction: Characterised the failure with probes rather than guessing; results kept on disk unmodified (archived to prior-invalid-run/ on the VPS) and clearly reported as invalid for the Jev strategies.
preventive_action: A smoke test must mirror the EXACT production request shape - assert on the real payload, not a convenient variant.

Measure decision-level capability, not just wire compatibility, before adopting a substitute runtime: include a state-discrimination test (two opposite states must yield different answers) and an order-swap test (swapping option order must not change the answer).
Gate long runs on a degeneracy check: after a small sample (e.g. 100 calls), abort if one class/option exceeds ~95% of answers or if confidence is pinned near ~0.
Document the substitution deviation (TypeSafe Jev -> Laya) and its required call-shape adaptation in the study record before any re-run.
secondary_failure: The original single-process run had in-memory-only caches and wrote artifacts only at completion, so the mid-run abort discarded all Jev inference work. Fixed: caches persist per (pair,date) to cache/*.json and the run is shardable/resumable.

correction_2026-09-26.note: The root cause above was REFINED after the first fix attempt. The original write-up over-attributed the degeneracy to a request-shape (first-option) bias. A 2x2 isolation experiment (12 payloads on production-style prompts) and a checkpoint probe show that is only part of the story.
refined_findings: REGIME question: returns a CONSTANT 'TRENDING' regardless of option order AND regardless of state (a strongly mean-reverting state also answered TRENDING, confidence 0.59-0.79, in both criteria wordings and both orders). So it is NOT order bias - the model has no discriminative signal for this question.

DIRECTION question with numeric-only prompts: answers follow option ORDER (up-state -> UP when UP listed first, DOWN when DOWN listed first; down-state -> UP when UP listed first, DOWN when DOWN listed first), i.e. no signal.
Instruction shape (dict vs string) mattered only for the probe whose state carried an explicit directional sentence, which is not the production prompt.
Answer distribution across the completed 15h run (100% TRENDING; 99% up) is therefore a capability failure of the substitute, not merely a wire-format defect.

A checkpoint probe on the fine-tuned 'typed-decisions' checkpoint had to be abandoned: requesting it loaded a second 421M model and drove the 3.3 GiB box into swap (3.1 GiB swap in use). Labelled as a resource failure, server recovered by restart. Note: that checkpoint is fine-tuned for invoice/security/CS/agent-trace workflows, not FX.
correction_2026-09-26.process_win: The fidelity probe + degeneracy gate added after the first invalid run caught the defect in about one minute and refused to start a second 15h run; the gate and cache-sanity guard both behaved as designed.
correction_2026-09-26.conclusion: Laya as shipped is not a usable substitute for Jev on this task. Local options are exhausted; the faithful paths are a fine-tuned checkpoint (needs labels + GPU time) or the real TypeSafe Jev (needs credits).
